items.prompt: Can a digital signal be copied exactly?
Do digital signals resist noise well?

steps: Digital signals resist noise better than analog.

items.prompt: Name one advantage of digital signals.
items.answer: Exact copying (or noise resistance, or error correction)

items.prompt: Why do digital copies not lose quality?
items.answer: The exact 0s and 1s are copied each time

items.prompt: Is music today usually stored digitally or analog?
What values does a digital signal use?
Do analog copies tend to degrade?
Name a wave used to carry signals.
items.answer: Radio waves (or light in fiber optics)

items.prompt: Explain why digital signals resist noise better.
items.answer: Small noise usually does not change which of the two values it is

steps: Two distinct values resist small noise.

items.prompt: Explain why digital music stays high quality over copies.
items.answer: Its 0s and 1s copy exactly, so quality is not lost

items.prompt: Evaluate: analog is always better than digital for information.
items.answer: Wrong; digital usually has advantages like exact copying and noise resistance

items.prompt: Why is error correction easier with digital signals?
items.answer: The distinct values make errors easy to detect and fix

items.prompt: Give one reason pictures are stored digitally today.
items.answer: Digital pictures can be copied exactly and resist noise

steps: Digital keeps pictures exact and clear.
